title: Animal models for depression-like and anxiety-like behavior
protocol: Fill a 19 cm diameter glass cylinder with water to a height of 10 cm, maintaining the temperature between 23-25°C.
Orient the camera for a horizontal view of the cylinder.
Place a sheet of cardboard between two beakers so mice cannot see each other.
Display coded animal identification numbers on videotape to allow blind scoring.
Dry the mouse in a drying cage using paper towels and heat lamps after swimming.
Use the same conditions as Day 1 for the second session.
Perform drug infusions in the morning before placing mice in water tanks four hours later.
Place mice into the swimming chambers for 15 minutes, videotaping their behavior.
Score recorded behavior to quantify immobility.
Conduct a single forced swim test session for non-infused animals (e.g., WT vs. HET).
Administer a second unilateral infusion one week after the forced swim test in cannulated mice.
Monitor locomotor activity four hours later using a video tracking system.
Calculate the distance traveled by each animal over a 10-minute period using Ethovision software.
Place a sheet of poster board between two tanks so rats cannot see each other.
Display coded animal identification numbers on videotape for blind scoring.
Place animals in a plexiglass tank filled with water to a height of 50-60 cm for 15 minutes.
Repeat day 1 setup.
Perform infusions in the morning.
Four hours after drug or vehicle infusions, measure locomotor activity by counting beam breaks over a 20-minute session.
Following locomotor activity assessment, perform the forced swim test where rats are placed in a water tank and videotaped for 10 minutes.
Score animals for immobility, swimming, and climbing using a sampling technique to rate predominant behavior over a 5-second interval for 10 minutes total.
Define immobility as absence of all movement except motions required to keep the head above the water.
Define climbing as thrashing movements along the sides of the water tank while swimming consists of horizontal motion moving from one quadrant to another.
Perform drug infusions in the morning.
Four hours post-infusion, administer a 6-minute tail suspension test.
Tape the tip of each tail using black electrical tape to a piece of Tygon tubing.
Suspend animal above the floor at 60 cm.
Videotape behavior.
Score the duration of immobility in 1-minute bins for 6 minutes.
Set lighting conditions to 40 lux (low lighting conditions) for EPM testing.
Place animal in the center platform of the Elevated Plus Maze (EPM).
Behavior videotaped for 5 minutes.
Score entries into dark arms, entries into light arms, time in light arms.
Perform Open Field Test (OFT) 2 days following EPM.
Administer mouse infusions prior to placing them into the center of a Plexiglas box.
Record distance moved and time spent in the entire open field or in a 25 cm x 25 cm center area using EthoVision pro video tracking system and software.
Expose mice to sweetened milk in their home cage for ~1-2 hr sessions for 3 days.
Score latency to drink from sweetened milk bottles in the home cage on the fourth day under dim lighting.
Perform drug infusions followed by measuring latencies to drink the sweetened milk in a novel cage on the fifth day under bright lighting.
Compare drinking latencies between the home cage and the novel cage.
